basis: The printing heads this gloss 'VERS. 40.' and it opens 'Vers. 40. Aestu urebar et gelu. Uno verbo, quod est urebar, ad duo contraria respondit,'. The printing's caput and the lemma's own words, matched against the Clementine, name the same chapter.
date_basis: Remigius taught at Reims and then at Paris and died about 908. His scriptural commentaries are products of that teaching and are not separately dated; the range covers the years in which he taught. The date is the writing, not Migne's 1853 printing.
text: Vers. 40. Aestu urebar et gelu. Uno verbo, quod est urebar, ad duo contraria respondit, ad aestum et ad gelu, quia unus effectus est caloris et frigoris.
